passage.title: Ice cream, sunburn and a lot of patience
passage.subtitle: Kitti Szabó, 18, describes her first real summer job

blocks.text: Last June, I started looking for a summer job because I wanted to save money for a driving course. My cousin had worked at an ice-cream stand in Balatonfüred the year before, and she told me they always needed students. I sent an email to the owner, Mr Kovács, and two days later I had an interview – on the phone, while he was serving customers.

I worked there for nine weeks, from the beginning of July until the end of August. My shift usually started at ten in the morning and finished at six in the evening, five days a week. At the weekends, when the town was full of tourists, we sometimes stayed open until ten at night. I earned 1,800 forints an hour, plus tips, which were often surprisingly good.

The work was harder than I expected. On hot days, the queue was sometimes thirty metres long, and everybody wanted their ice cream immediately. Scooping ice cream for eight hours is tiring for your arms – after the first week, my right wrist hurt so much that I had to wear a bandage. I also had to clean the freezers every evening, which was the part of the job I liked least.

The best thing was the people. I worked with three other students, and we became really good friends. We invented names for the regular customers, like 'Mr Pistachio', an old man who came every day at exactly four o'clock and always ordered the same flavour. I also practised my English and German a lot, because many of the tourists came from Austria and Germany.

I learnt a lot of things that you can't learn at school. I learnt to stay calm when customers were rude, to count change quickly, and to smile even when I was tired. Mr Kovács was strict but fair: if you were late, you had to stay longer, but if you worked really hard, he gave you an extra day off.
By the end of the summer, I had saved enough for the driving course and still had some money left for a new phone. Mr Kovács has already asked me to come back next year – and I've said yes.
